plan.title: feat(design-critique): the arc is the recommended step before ingest for every issue; skip only with a recorded not-warranted line

narratives.Description: feat(design-critique): the arc is the recommended step before ingest for every issue; skip only with a recorded not-warranted line
narratives.Overview:
## TL;DR

Every issue, maintainer or consumer, gets the design-critique arc before `issue:ingest`, or a recorded `design-critique: not warranted, because …` line. No subset, no qualifier, no "ordinary scope" exemption. This is a posture change on instruction surfaces plus one advisory line at the ingest chokepoint; it is not an engine gate and ADR-005 is unchanged. It makes the operator bar already recorded on #3995 (comment 5574437975) the deposited default for everyone, and absorbs #4229 resolution 5.

## What "all the time" means, concretely

1. **Trigger:** any GitHub issue about to be ingested. Not "mechanism-shaped", not "design-type". The `mechanism-shaped` stamp keeps its ADR-005 role (what the advisory judgment gate matches); it no longer scopes the recommendation.
2. **Exemption:** exactly one — a recorded clearance line of the existing shape `design-critique: not warranted, because …` (parser `DESIGN_CRITIQUE_CLEARANCE_SHAPE`, `packages/core/src/orchestration/judgment-policy.ts`). Silence, "ordinary playable", "chore", or an unlabelled issue is not a skip. Chores pay one line, not an arc.
3. **Default spend:** N=1 open critique. Never a panel by default.
4. **Timing fence kept:** the arc belongs at planning. The skill's "do not trigger on ordinary implement, build, or swarm work" stays, because that fence is about *when*, not *which issues*.
5. **Scopes with no GitHub issue:** out of reach until #5486 (open, in active) lands "run an arc on an xBRIEF when no GitHub issue exists". This issue names that dependency and does not pretend to cover it.

## Why now

- Operator bar on #3995 (2026-09-07): "run an arc when possible; skip only with a recorded `design-critique: not warranted, because …`. Silence or 'ordinary playable' is not a skip." Two weeks of universal manual practice: most arcs find a problem; skipping usually ships a bad lean.
- 2026-10-17/18: three N=1 critic passes on one proposal set blocked five central claims that would otherwise have been filed (#5694 class). Repeated use makes the pattern obvious: the arc is the step that catches the bad lean before code.
- Consumer field report #4229: a consumer treated the arc as n/a for an "ordinary playable scope"; the deposited text allowed it.
- Today the deposited posture is opt-in. The skill description reads "Use when the operator asks … Do NOT trigger on ordinary implement, build, or swarm work"; no always-on surface names the arc; `issue:ingest` returns `not-in-arc` silently for an unarced issue (`assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest`, `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:2385`, only throws on `blocked`).

## Scope

Instruction surfaces (unconditional wording on each):

1. **Skill posture.** `deft-directive-design-critique` description and § When to Use (pack source `content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json`, `task packs:render`): the arc is the recommended step before `issue:ingest` for every issue; the only skip is the recorded clearance line; the build/swarm timing fence stays.
2. **Managed AGENTS.md pointer.** One line in `content/templates/agents-entry.md` inside the 135-byte headroom (`agentsMdBudget.absoluteMaxBytes` 28400; no ratchet raise, #3735), propagated by `task agents:refresh`, gated by `agents_entry_contract` (#1309). Shape: before `issue:ingest`, arc or record `design-critique: not warranted, because …`. Supersedes the "offer" pointer drafted as NEW-C1 in the delivery coverage tracker.
3. **Session routing / Plan order.** `content/commands.md` § Session routing: triage write-back → arc or recorded skip → `issue:ingest` → scope. Same line in the managed Session routing card if bytes allow.
4. **Setup close-out.** `deft-directive-setup` tells the consumer the arc is the default planning step and shows the skip line. Prose only; no `judgmentGates` writer.

The one surface that fires every time (Rule Authority: prefer a verb over prose):

5. **Ingest advisory.** In `issue:ingest`, when `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` returns `not-in-arc` and neither the issue body nor any comment carries a clearance-shaped line, print one advisory line naming the skill and the skip form. Exit 0. Never blocks. Reuses the existing verdict and parser; adds no new classifier. (This is the ingest-advisory road the NEW-C1 critic weighed and set aside only because the pointer was cheaper; with an unconditional recommendation the chokepoint line is what makes "every issue" true in practice.)

Measurement, so the posture can be judged later rather than argued:

6. **Skip-rate visibility.** The advisory emits a counted event (existing run-summary / events stream) distinguishing `arced`, `skipped-recorded`, `neither`. This feeds the per-arc series #3995 still owes and #3923's measurement.

## Recorded departure, stated so it is not silent

- #3578 lists "a review agent on every triage" as explicitly rejected, and ADR-005 § refusals 3 says voluntary critiques are "not precedent for always-fire". Both are about the engine: an auto-firing gate or an auto-dispatched reviewer. This issue changes neither. It sets the *instruction* posture to recommended-by-default with a cheap recorded opt-out, which ADR-005 already allows as voluntary spend. The operator made that call on #3995 after measured practice; this issue deposits it. If the skip-rate series later shows the recommendation is mostly skipped, that is evidence for #3995, not a reason to hide the recommendation.

## Not in scope (owned elsewhere)

- Engine refusal of unarced work, auto-stamping `mechanism-shaped`, auto-dispatch, or an ADR-005 amendment: #3995, #3923, #3578. ADR-005 § refusals 3 stands.
- A `judgmentGates` policy writer or promote-time enforcement ladder (#1511 holds `verify:judgment-gates` at `hold`; `--enforce` is a no-op on the declared/review entry).
- Arcs on issue-less scopes: #5486.

## Acceptance

- Skill description and § When to Use carry the unconditional posture and the skip form; no "mechanism-shaped" qualifier on the recommendation.
- Managed AGENTS.md carries the pointer; `verify:agents-md-budget` green, no ratchet raise.
- `commands.md` Session routing names the order.
- `issue:ingest` prints the advisory on `not-in-arc` with no clearance line; exit 0; one unit test for each of the three states.
- Skip-rate events present in the run-summary stream.
- Existing contracts green (`design_critique_contract.test.ts`, `skill-external-fetch-gate.test.ts`); one new contract assertion that the rendered skill description contains the skip form.
- Cross-link comment on #4229 (resolution 5 delivered here) and on #3995 (operator bar deposited; series input added).
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Critic verdict (process-only, pre-issue)

Partial. The pointer (item 2) went through an N=1 pre-issue critic as NEW-C1 of the delivery coverage tracker at `83de55b393b2f03b6bd7445edaa3aa8bb4a31f4c`: a specGuard-style enforcement follow-up and a setup `judgmentGates` offer were struck; byte budget and owner #4229 were set. The unconditional posture (items 1, 3, 4), the ingest advisory (5) and the skip-rate events (6) have not been critiqued. By this issue's own rule, this issue gets the arc before ingest.

## Relates

#3995 (operator bar; round-1 F6 "consumer skip is an instruction gap"), #4229 (resolution 5, dominated here), #5486 (issue-less scopes), #3923, #3578, #4071, #5326, #5694, #3735, #1309. ADR-005 unchanged.

🤖 Filed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
